description: Language-agnostic vectors of the axial twist (`twistDeg`). The figure is the rig of the sample figure standing at a hip height of 0.96 m: the torso origin is at (0, 1.06) pointing up, arm-l hangs from (0, 1.48) pointing down (0.6 m), shank-l ends at the ankle (0, 0.08) where foot-l (0.22 m) points forward. After its own sagittal rotation (and spread) a bone turns about its own longitudinal axis by twistDeg, accumulating down the chain; positive twist turns the local +y axis of the bone towards the right of the asset, so a bone pointing up turns counter-clockwise seen from above (forward goes to the left) and a bone pointing down turns clockwise. Elevation, front and plan are the orthographic projections of the same three-dimensional chain. Hand computations: the arm raised forward (angleDeg 90, its tip 0.6 m ahead at rest of the twist) on a torso twisted by tau points 0.6*cos(tau) ahead and 0.6*sin(tau) to the left at height 1.48: tau = 45 deg gives 0.424264 ahead and 0.424264 left, tau = 90 deg gives 0 ahead and 0.6 left, tau = 180 deg gives 0.6 behind and 0 sideways. Half way of a transition from standing to that pose (torso 45 deg, arm 45 deg) the arm direction is -0.7071*up - 0.7071*v' = (0.5, -0.7071, 0.5), so its tip is at (0.3, 1.055736) and 0.3 m left; its bone normal projects to (0.5, 0.7071), which gives the elevation extents. A shank twisted by -90 deg turns its foot (0.22 m) sideways to the left: the projected tip stays at the ankle and lies 0.22 m left, so the front view grows outwards by 0.22 m and the plan view turns into a lateral sliver. Front and plan shapes are authored in the rest pose and move by the projected travel of their bone plus its lateral position (see the lateral-spread vectors). Extents are compared within extentToleranceM (1 mm); the transition case compares the vertical and lateral extents only because a transition advances the forward position slightly. Rigid shapes of a twisted subtree turn exactly about the vertical: the rigid block on the torso (plan: 0.1 to 0.3 ahead, 0.1 either side; front: 0.1 to 0.3 lateral, height 1.0 to 1.1 at rest) is rotated about the torso axis in plan by tau, (x, z) -> (x cos tau - z sin tau, x sin tau + z cos tau): tau = 45 deg gives 0 to 0.282843 both ways, tau = 90 deg gives x -0.1 to 0.1 and z 0.1 to 0.3, tau = 180 deg gives x -0.3 to -0.1 and z -0.1 to 0.1; in front the lateral coordinate becomes z cos tau (0.070711 to 0.212132 at 45 deg, 0 at 90 deg, -0.3 to -0.1 at 180 deg) and the height is the rest height plus the standing travel of 0.96 m. A twist of the shank leaves the torso block where it was. The shapes of the bones that twist are centred on the bone (arm-follow and foot-follow lateral -0.05 to 0.05). The arm raised forward under a torso twist tau has the frame u = (cos tau, 0, sin tau), w = (-sin tau, 0, cos tau) and stays at height 1.48, so its front rectangle (a = 0.52 - y, c = lateral) has lateral' = a sin tau + c cos tau: -0.035355 to 0.459619 at 45 degrees, 0 to 0.6 at 90 degrees, -0.05 to 0.05 at 180 degrees. At the half way of the transition u = (0.5, -0.7071, 0.5) and w = (-0.7071, 0, 0.7071): lateral' = 0.5 a + 0.7071 c from -0.035355 to 0.335355, height' = 1.48 - 0.7071 a from 1.055736 to 1.48. The foot twisted sideways by the shank (u = (0, 0, 1), w = (-1, 0, 0)) maps the plan point (x, y) to (-y, x): x -0.05 to 0.05, y 0 to 0.22. Solids on a twisted or spread subtree use the full 3D frame. Extruded: the profile (a along the bone, b along its normal) swept along the lateral axis c from z0 to z1 (rest lateral of the bone origin subtracted), P = O + a u + b v + c w, projected to the view and hulled. Torso slab (a 0 to 0.45, b -0.1 to 0.1, z -0.2 to 0.2, torso origin (0, 1.06)): twisted by tau the torso frame is u = (0, 1, 0), v = (-cos tau, 0, -sin tau), w = (-sin tau, 0, cos tau), so plan x = -b cos tau - c sin tau and plan y = -b sin tau + c cos tau: tau = 90 gives x = -c (-0.2 to 0.2) and y = -b (-0.1 to 0.1), tau = 45 gives 0.7071 (b + c) and 0.7071 (c - b), both -0.212132 to 0.212132. Revolved: the circle of radius b (the distance of the profile point from the axis) at the height a along the axis, normal n, projects to half-width b sqrt(1 - n_k^2) per coordinate k. Drum (a 0.1 to 0.4, b 0 to 0.1) on the torso tilted back by 14 degrees: n = u = (-sin 14, cos 14, 0) = (-0.241922, 0.970296, 0), centres (-0.241922 a, 1.06 + 0.970296 a, 0): plan x from -0.241922 * 0.4 - 0.1 * 0.970296 = -0.193799 to -0.241922 * 0.1 + 0.0970296 = 0.072838, plan y +-0.1; front lateral +-0.1, front y from 1.06 + 0.970296 * 0.1 - 0.1 * 0.241922 = 1.132838 to 1.06 + 0.970296 * 0.4 + 0.0241922 = 1.47231. Lid (the arm, rest axis down, raised 105 degrees on the torso twisted by 90 degrees): the arm frame is u = (0, 0.258819, 0.965926), v = (0, 0.965926, -0.258819), w = (-1, 0, 0), the revolved axis (the carried vertical) n = -u = (0, -0.258819, -0.965926); centres (0, 1.48 + 0.258819 a, 0.965926 a), a 0.1 to 0.5, radius b up to 0.1: front lateral from 0.096593 - 0.1 * 0.258819 = 0.070711 to 0.482963 + 0.025882 = 0.508845, front y from 1.505882 - 0.0965926 = 1.409289 to 1.60941 + 0.0965926 = 1.706003; plan x +-0.1. Extruded lid slab (a 0.1 to 0.5, b -0.05 to 0.05, c -0.1 to 0.1): x = -c, lateral = 0.965926 a - 0.258819 b (0.083652 to 0.495904), y = 1.48 + 0.258819 a + 0.965926 b (1.457586 to 1.657706). Single 3D path: the foot turned sideways by the shank twist keeps no width in front, only the 0.22 m it extends (front lateral 0 to 0.22). Elevation solids: a solid on an elevation shape is the same 3D definition projected to the side view: the torso slab twisted by tau has the elevation x = -b cos tau - c sin tau and y = 1.06 + a, so 0.2 m (-0.1 to 0.1) upright, 0.424264 m at 45 degrees and 0.4 m (-0.2 to 0.2) at 90 degrees, and the drum (revolved) stays 0.2 m wide in every twist. Plain sagittal lid: the arm raised 105 degrees without twist has the frame u = (0.965926, 0.258819, 0), v = (-0.258819, 0.965926, 0), the carried vertical axis n = -u = (-0.965926, -0.258819, 0) and the circles of radius b (up to 0.1) at the centres (0.965926 a, 1.48 + 0.258819 a, 0); the side and plan half-widths are b * 0.258819 along x and b * 0.965926 along y, so the revolved lid spans x 0.070711 to 0.508845 and y 1.409289 to 1.706003 (the former vertical axis gave a 0.2 m wide disc), and the extruded lid slab x = 0.965926 a - 0.258819 b (0.083652 to 0.495904), y = 1.48 + 0.258819 a + 0.965926 b (1.457586 to 1.657706). One outline per solid: the projection of a solid is the union of the swept edges (shapely unary_union equivalent), never a ring per profile edge. Concave profile: the L-shaped bracket (a along the bone, b across; the vertical bar a 0 to 0.05, b -0.1 to 0.1, the foot a 0 to 0.45, b -0.1 to -0.05, area 0.03 m2) extruded z -0.2 to 0.2 on the torso twisted 90 degrees projects to the front as (z, y) = (-b, 1.06 + a): the mirrored L, a single non-convex ring of 6 vertices and area 0.03 m2 (the lateral sweep c runs along the forward axis and does not show); twisted 45 degrees (z = -0.7071 b + 0.7071 c, swept 0.282843 horizontally) the horizontal slices are 0.141421 + 0.282843 = 0.424264 wide for a 0 to 0.05 and 0.035355 + 0.282843 = 0.318198 wide for a 0.05 to 0.45: area 0.05 * 0.424264 + 0.4 * 0.318198 = 0.148492 m2. An upright extruded rectangle (the slab 0.45 by 0.2 m, 0.4 m deep) is exactly its rectangle: one ring of 4 vertices, area 0.18 m2 in front (0.4 wide by 0.45 high), 0.08 in plan (0.2 by 0.4) and 0.09 in elevation (0.2 by 0.45); twisted 90 degrees the front slab is 0.2 by 0.45 = 0.09 m2. Depth of flat shapes: a plan shape is carried at the height of the middle of its elevation twin (same id, same bone) at rest, a front shape at its forward position. The pedestal (elevation twin at a = 0.9 to 1.0, rest height 1.05 m, torso origin 0.1 m) in plan at forward -0.05 to 0.05: torso tilted back by 14 degrees, u = (-0.241922, 0.970296), v = (-0.970296, -0.241922): x' = -0.241922 * 0.95 - 0.970296 * (-x)... = -0.229826 + 0.970296 x, so -0.278342 to -0.18131. Without a twin the depth is the bone origin (x' = 0.970296 x); author such a part as a solid. Tilted rest axis: a revolved solid revolves about the longitudinal axis of its axis bone (its own rest direction, carried by the pose), not about the vertical. Hub: the foot (rest axis horizontal, forward, origin (0, 0.08) standing), profile a 0 to 0.22 along the bone, b 0 to 0.1 up: circles of radius b at the centres (a, 0.08, 0) with the normal (1, 0, 0): front disc of radius 0.1 (lateral -0.1 to 0.1, height -0.02 to 0.18), plan and elevation x 0 to 0.22 by +-0.1. (A pose tilting the foot would also change the grounding of the figure, so the tilted-pose revolve is covered by the drum on the torso tilted back 14 degrees.)

cases.name: a torso twisted 45 degrees turns the forward arm 0.424264 m to the left and shortens it in the elevation
a torso twisted 90 degrees turns the arm fully to the left: it vanishes in the elevation and reaches 0.6 m sideways in front
a torso twisted 180 degrees turns the arm to the back and leaves no lateral reach
a transition half way interpolates the twist (torso 45 degrees, arm 45 degrees)
a shank twisted by -90 degrees turns its foot sideways: it grows outwards in front and becomes a lateral sliver in plan
an extruded slab on a torso twisted 90 degrees swaps its depth and width: 0.4 m wide in plan, 0.2 m in front
an extruded slab on a torso twisted 45 degrees is 0.424264 m across in both views
a revolved drum on a torso tilted back by 14 degrees (and twisted) revolves about the tilted axis: its front circles flatten by sin 14 and its plan reaches back
a lid opened 105 degrees on a twisted body: its revolved part turns about the tilted axis and its extruded part is swept along the turned lateral axis
an upright torso: the extruded slab and the revolved drum project to their authored profile in the side view and swap nothing
a lid opened 105 degrees by a plain sagittal rotation (no spread, no twist) revolves about its tilted axis too: a dome of 0.438 m by 0.297 m instead of a vertical disc

a flat plan part high on a tilted bone is carried at the height of its elevation twin: the 0.1 m pedestal at the top of the torso tilted back 14 degrees shifts back by 0.95 sin 14 deg = 0.229826 m, not as if it sat at the origin

a body of revolution on a bone whose rest axis is horizontal revolves about that axis (the foot axis points forward): end-on it is a disc of radius 0.1 m in front, a 0.22 m by 0.2 m band in the other views

frames.name: arm at torso twist 270 (a joint with whole turns)
arm at torso twist 360 (a joint with whole turns)

limits.name: a twist of 90 degrees on a revolute joint is allowed
a twist of 180 degrees is the largest allowed
a twist above 180 degrees is refused
a twist of 300 degrees is allowed on a joint with twistMaxDeg 360
a twist above twistMaxDeg is refused
a twist of -300 degrees is allowed on a joint with twistMinDeg -360
a twist of -190 degrees is refused when twistMinDeg is not given
